SddRoot.keywords: root, portal, vision, scope-graph, idempotent, project-setup, infra-bootstrap
SddRoot.Mission:
Owner of `specs/README.md` — the Project Portal: Vision + Scope Graph + Scopes table. Idempotent: runs any number of times to refine vision, extend the graph, or bootstrap the first infra-base spec. Loaded lazily by the router; the router-core beliefs it relies on are declared in `BeliefState deps` (inherited, not repeated).
Input — operator intent at project level. Output: - `specs/README.md` with Vision + Scope Graph + Scopes table. - Optional minimal `specs/infra-base/infra-base.spec.md` when the operator declared tooling.
When the portal is absent, root reads the probe facts already in the `sdd-state` snapshot: a greenfield repo (no code) is initialized here; a repo that already holds code is handed to the from-code recovery branch (`discover-from-code`) — root never invents a vision over code that already exists.
Out of scope: design of any individual scope (its vision, architecture, requirements, modules) — that is the scope branch. Root writes only the project-level map.

BeliefState.deps: AX_OPERATOR_LANGUAGE, AX_TOOL_INVOCATION, AX_OPERATOR_DIALOGUE_STYLE, AX_DIALOGUE_DISCIPLINE, AX_OPERATOR_SAFEGUARD, AX_NO_PROCESS_NARRATION, AX_STATELESS_ARTIFACT, AX_READER_WITHOUT_SESSION_CONTEXT

SddRoot.BeliefState:
Inherited from the loading directive (already in context): QUESTION_RULE_SLIM
The `root` flow is the primary owner of `specs/README.md`. Other flows MUST NOT rewrite this file. Reads are unrestricted.
Explicit, narrow exceptions (append-only edits permitted, no rewrites): - The `scope` flow creating a brand-new scope MAY append a placeholder row to the Scopes table tagged `🚧 (awaiting root sync)` so the new scope is visible in the Portal before the next `root` run. - The `module` flow MUST NOT touch this file; its Portal-level summaries are appended only to its scope spec.
Any other edit by another flow → audit finding `STALE_AFTER_PIVOT` or `EXECUTION_LOG_INCOMPLETE` depending on context. The next `root` run reconciles placeholders into full rows.
`setup` has no hard modes (no greenfield / extension / pivot). - Portal absent → create from scratch. - Portal present → read and propose updates derived from intake; operator dictates what to change.
No silent assumptions: empty intake against an existing Portal → HALT `H_NO_INTENT` («what are we changing today?»).
Scope Graph is a directed dependency graph. Rules: - Edge A→B means «scope A depends-on scope B»: A inherits B's effective rules in the cascade and may consume B's contracts. - Cycle in the graph → `H_CYCLE_IN_GRAPH` (abort). - scope-type constraints: `infrastructure` and `interface` scopes are typically leaves (depend only on other infra / interface). `product` and `library` scopes depend on infra + interface. - The graph is rendered as a Mermaid `graph TD` block inside the Portal.
When proposing scope or module candidates, draw the boundary along three axes, never mixed into one unit: data / domain (business rules, state, persistence) ↔ UI / presentation (view, rendering, user interaction) ↔ infrastructure (transport, deployment, third-party wiring). A candidate spanning two axes is a signal to split it, not a shortcut to take. A shared core is extracted from these axes only once ≥2 real consumers need it — never speculatively (`AX_YAGNI_OVERENGINEERING_GUARD`); a single consumer stays inline.
If the operator declares basic tooling (package manager, type-checker, linter) in intake, the `root` flow materializes a minimal `specs/infra-base/infra-base.spec.md` with scope-type=infrastructure: Vision (one sentence) + Tool Stack (table with tool names only, no Decision Log yet). The full Decision Log appears when the operator runs the `infra` flow on infra-base.
The minimal bootstrap intentionally bypasses the full `infra` flow — it only locks the tool choice without the Design Variants ritual.
Scopes table in the Portal: each row = link to the scope spec + scope-type + status emoji + one-line description. - ✅ — spec exists and is approved. - 🚧 — spec being authored / `discovery` not yet run. - Status is derived purely from the presence of `specs//.spec.md`.
The `## Vision` section in the Portal is present only when the project contains at least one product or library scope. For tooling-only repos (sandboxes, infra repos) the Vision section is omitted.
Every non-obvious decision → a Decision Log entry in `DECISION_LOG_ENTRY_FORMAT` — one line, the expanded part in parentheses: `-DL-N — (почему: …; отвергнуто: …; риск: …)`; IDs are stable. Non-obvious only (`AX_DECISION_LOG_NON_OBVIOUS`): a pick already recorded in the spec's own tables is never duplicated as a DL row. Which decisions qualify and which Decision Log receives the entry are specified per directive.
A mutation is not done until its scope passes the mechanical check. Any flow that creates or evolves an artifact under a scope — spec, module, ticket, DAG, tracker — closes by running `sdd-check` on the affected scope (`sdd-check --all specs/`; portal, task-DAG, tracker, or cross-scope work → `sdd-check --all .`) and resolving or consciously deferring every finding before handing off.

ChatProtocol.Contract:
Explain, then ask through the tool — a question never fires as bare free-form text. A `### 💡 <О чём решаем>` section header names the decision in plain words, without numbering and without semantic question IDs; under it, ordinary language explains the question BEFORE any tool call fires — the context, the real options, and a recommendation gated by `AX_DIVERGE_BEFORE_RECOMMEND` (low-stakes: a direct pick is fine; high-stakes / architecture: do not pre-anchor one option — lay out the strongest candidates, a tail one included, or pair the recommendation with its strongest rival and the reason it might win instead). Only once the explanation stands does `AskUserQuestion` fire; its option list mirrors the printed order, short labels only — the argument itself lives in the message, never moved into the tool call.
Batching rule: one `AskUserQuestion` call may carry several questions ONLY when they are mutually independent — answering one does not change the meaning or the options of another (several facets of one single complex decision qualify as one batched call). Dependent questions, and any interview sequence, go one call at a time: compose the next question only after the previous answer is in.
Channel: use `AskUserQuestion` whenever the tool is available. When it is not, fall back to plain text carrying the same shape — the explanation, then an explicit list of named options the operator can answer by name; skipping the explanation and firing a bare list of options is itself the violation this contract forbids (`H_UNFORMATTED_ASK`).
Low-stakes — a recommendation is allowed, but only as the result of `AX_DIVERGE_BEFORE_RECOMMEND` (not the first typical answer):
Пример — иллюстрация формата, не задание:
### 💡 Куда положить ресёрч-документ Документ можно держать рядом со спекой — виден в контексте скоупа, проще найти, пока читаешь её — или в общем каталоге ресёрчей, если он пригодится за пределами одного скоупа; для разового ресёрча под конкретную спеку разница небольшая. ✅ **Рядом со спекой** `[specs//research/]` — виден в контексте скоупа, не потеряется. Иначе: - **Общий каталог** `[docs/research/]` — _за: виден без привязки к одному скоупу · против: сложнее понять, к какой спеке относится_
(AskUserQuestion: «Рядом со спекой (рекомендую)» · «Общий каталог»)
High-stakes / architecture — do NOT pre-anchor one pick. List the strongest candidates (include a non-obvious / tail one) with «за / против» and let the operator choose; or give a recommendation only alongside its strongest alternative and the reason it might win:
Пример — иллюстрация формата, не задание:
### 💡 Граница нового скоупа Функциональность можно оформить отдельным скоупом или модулем внутри существующего — от этого зависит, где заводить спеку и как считать её границы; пре-анкоринг здесь дороже, чем в низкоставочном случае. - **Отдельный скоуп** `[new-scope]` — _за: чистая граница, не тащит чужие инварианты · против: больше координации между скоупами_ - **Модуль внутри существующего скоупа** `[module-in-scope]` — _за: меньше накладных расходов, общий контекст уже есть · против: граница скоупа расползается со временем_ - **Отложить решение до следующей итерации** `[defer]` — нетипичный вариант, но снимает риск закрепить границу раньше, чем видно реальное использование
(AskUserQuestion: «Отдельный скоуп» · «Модуль внутри существующего» · «Отложить (нетипичный)»)
A plain binary question needs no list — recommendation + inline alternative, still explained before the call:
Пример — иллюстрация формата, не задание:
### 💡 Нужен ли отдельный interface-скоуп Все текущие потребители — web; про API и будущих клиентов явно не говорили. ✅ **Пока не выделять** — можно добавить позже без миграции. _или сразу выделить, если API уже в планах?_
(AskUserQuestion: «Пока не выделять (рекомендую)» · «Выделить сразу»)
A counter-question in reply to a gate is a side-dive, not a rejection: (a) answer the counter-question in full, on its own merits, before returning to the gate; (b) bring the gate back exactly once, marked as a repeat pass, enriched with whatever the counter-question surfaced — «повторяю вопрос» plus a fact or option the side-dive added (e.g. operator asked "как ты делаешь ресёрч?" → the repeat pass adds an option «сначала ресёрч, потом решаем»); a verbatim repeat of the first gate carries no delta and is itself the violation. (c) if the operator answers the repeat pass with another counter-question instead of a pick, do not fire a third pass — stop and ask directly what is blocking the decision.

SddRoot.HaltConditions: | 🛑 ID | Trigger | |---|---| | `H_NO_INTENT` | Operator invoked the root flow with empty intake against an existing Portal | | `H_CYCLE_IN_GRAPH` | Scope Graph contains a cycle (detected by `sdd-check`) | | `H_SCOPE_VS_MODULE_AMBIGUITY` | Operator labels as «scope» something that resembles a module | | `H_OPERATOR_REJECT` | Operator rejected Vision, Scope Graph, or the final Portal |

Step.Goal: Determine today's change set from state.
Step.Action: State from the router (`sdd-state`) already reports whether `specs/README.md` exists. - Absent → no portal yet: read `CODE` from the `sdd-state` output already in context — the probe (`CODE`/`INFRA`, code-dirs, configs) is part of the default snapshot; do NOT call `sdd-state` a second time for it. - `CODE=absent` (empty / only package.json) → **greenfield init**. The operator already saw the `sdd-state` card, shown verbatim as its own fenced unit by the router's SHOW-gate, and, for empty intake, confirmed «Создать проект» at the router's entry Ask (`AX_DIALOGUE_DISCIPLINE`) — the interview opens HERE, never before that card and never as free text dumped into the reply. An interview question that precedes the card, or that re-summarizes it instead of the router having shown it, violates the same gate the router enforces (`H_ASK_WITHOUT_CARD`) — a summary of the card is not the card. The project name is NOT asked here: default it silently to the repository folder's own name, kebab-case as-is, no invented embellishment — it then appears in every later show, and the operator may correct it inline in any free-text answer to STEP_1 or STEP_2 without a dedicated name question ever existing. One decision per question (`AX_OPERATOR_SAFEGUARD`): naming is resolved silently here precisely so STEP_1 can ask vision alone and STEP_2 can ask scopes alone — never bundle name + vision + scopes into one opening question again. - `CODE=present` → **from-code recovery** — do NOT invent a vision over existing code: `READ_AND_USE_DIRECTIVE("ai/directives/sdd-v2/discover-from-code.directive.xml")`. - Present → empty intake → `H_NO_INTENT`; otherwise classify the change: vision / add scope / update graph / infra bootstrap. Root has no hard modes — create when absent, propose intake-derived updates when present, per `AX_IDEMPOTENT_MODES`.

Step.Goal: Lock the project-level Vision, routing every anchor of the operator's statement to the artifact that owns it.
Step.Action:
No product / library scope → skip Vision (`AX_VISION_ONLY_FOR_APPLICATION`). Else, on greenfield init (no Vision recorded yet), ask ONE open question through `AskUserQuestion` when available, otherwise `QUESTION_FORMAT`: «Что строим? Опиши замысел свободно.» with an escape option «Пока не знаю — предложи сам». Vision is the one field of genuine human intent in this step — the agent never fabricates it unasked, because a wrong guess here is an expensive semantic error to unwind later.
Once the operator answers, the agent does NOT compress the answer — it NORMALIZES it while ROUTING every semantic anchor to the artifact it actually belongs to; dropping an anchor is a loss, but filing it under the wrong artifact is a second, independent loss (a release boundary misread as the target state, or a target state watered down by a caveat that only applies to v1). Three anchor kinds, three homes: - **Target state** — what the finished thing does, for whom, the full shape of the outcome → Vision, worded as the COMPLETE goal with no release caveat folded in. «Синхронизация между устройствами» stays the target even when v1 ships without it. - **Deferred / release-boundary decision** — «в v1 без бэкенда», «пока без синхронизации», «не сейчас» → a `AX_DECISION_LOG_REQUIRED` entry in `DECISION_LOG_ENTRY_FORMAT`, marked deferred. Example: operator says «v1 строго local-only, без бэкенда» while the goal is full sync → Vision keeps «полная синхронизация между устройствами» as the target, and the Decision Log gets `-DL-1 — v1 без бэкенда (почему: быстрее показать локальный сценарий; отложено до: этап синхронизации; риск: придётся менять модель хранения данных)`. - **Technical/stack preference** — a named framework, «готовый UIKit», a design-system pick → carried forward as intake for the step that actually owns implementation choices (STEP_2's scope-boundary call, STEP_3's tool-stack lock, or the later `scope`/`infra` session) — it never becomes a Vision sentence; Vision describes outcome, not toolchain.
Every anchor the operator actually said lands in exactly one of the three homes above — the reader test from `AX_READER_WITHOUT_SESSION_CONTEXT` (would a specialist with zero memory of this session understand and act on it?) applies to each home's own wording.
With anchors routed, close the remaining gaps in the Vision's own facets — for whom, the pain, the success criterion, the target state itself, guiding principles — through a microinterview that asks ONLY about facets the operator's words left open (`AX_SCALE_PROPORTIONAL_DEPTH`): a facet already covered by a routed anchor is never asked about again. Bundle every open facet into ONE `AskUserQuestion` call as independent questions — options drawn from real product practice plus the tool's own free-text slot for a custom answer, `multiSelect` where a facet genuinely allows more than one true answer. A rich statement closes most facets on its own, leaving 0-1 follow-up questions; a thin one-liner leaves several open, and the full round runs.
Assemble the structured Vision block from the routed target-state anchor plus the microinterview answers: one paragraph carrying the target state (no release caveats), followed by short strong-labelled sub-bullets — **Для кого**, **Боль**, **Успех**, **Принципы** — each filled from what the operator actually said, never fabricated for an unasked facet. Russian text quality follows `AX_OPERATOR_LANGUAGE` (flat, plain, no calque); the same bar audit checks later under `AX_LANGUAGE_QUALITY_CHECK` applies here at authoring time, not just at review time. The assembled block, and any Decision Log entries routed alongside it, are proposed back for confirm-or-edit — never treated as locked without that confirmation, opening with the recap per `UNDERSTANDING_BLOCK_FORMAT`: the routing above is exactly the misread risk that format exists to surface (a caveat filed as the target, an anchor sent to the wrong home) — name the riskiest routing call, tied to this confirm-or-edit. If the operator picks the escape option, draft a Vision candidate from whatever context already exists (project name, intake, README) and present it back the same way. On an idempotent update (a Vision already exists), propose an intake-derived revision instead of asking from scratch. Approval Check. STOP.

Step.Goal: Select which scopes exist, then place each by its relationships before its edges.
Step.Action: On greenfield init (graph still empty), propose scope candidates in ONE multiSelect `AskUserQuestion` call (`multiSelect: true`) derived from the just-locked Vision — never asked as free text first. Draw each candidate's boundary per `AX_SEPARATION_OF_CONCERNS` (data/domain ↔ UI/presentation ↔ infrastructure; a shared core only once ≥2 consumers need it): the product-scope (name derived from Vision, kebab-case), then `infra-base` tagged «(Recommended)» with description «гейты: type-check/test/lint — обязательна перед scaffold/execute», then `interface` / `library` candidates only when the Vision actually implies them. The operator clicks checkboxes rather than composing scope names from scratch; the tool's own free-text slot already covers a custom answer, so do not duplicate it as an extra bullet. Checking a box only registers that scope in the Scopes table — deep design of any one scope (its own vision, architecture, requirements, modules) stays out of this step and happens in its own later `scope` session, per the Mission's own boundary. For each scope now in play (freshly checked here, or already present on a later update), the relationship question comes FIRST (`AX_OPERATOR_SAFEGUARD`): who will depend on it, what it depends on, and whether it is cross-cutting (used by ≥2 scopes). Probe narrow framing — «авторизация только для web? а API / будущие клиенты?». The answer drives three things: the «scope vs module» test (a thing used inside one scope may be a module, not a scope → `H_SCOPE_VS_MODULE_AMBIGUITY`); the `depends-on` edges; and, when it is cross-cutting, a note that cross-scope scenarios or an interface scope may be needed. If the change REMOVES or RENAMES a scope, first surface what it orphans — its `specs//…` spec, tasks, and inbound references — and resolve with the operator (move / delete / repoint); never silently leave orphans. Then propose scope-type with rationale — edge semantics (A→B = A depends-on B), acyclicity, and scope-type constraints per `AX_SCOPE_GRAPH_DISCIPLINE` (a cycle → `H_CYCLE_IN_GRAPH`). Show the graph to the operator as a layered ASCII diagram — the dependency structure this renders is exactly the case `FLOW_DIAGRAM_WHEN` grants the one fenced block allowed inside an operator message for — sourced from the `[GRAPH]` block `sdd-state` already put in context (levels + edges) — never re-derive levels by re-reading the Portal, and never print the Mermaid `graph TD` into the chat message: that fenced block is file content, it belongs only inside `specs/README.md` (mermaid belongs to the file, printing it in chat is a display violation). Layout: one horizontal tier per level, stacked top → bottom in DESCENDING level order (highest level / widest consumers on top, the level-0 foundation on the bottom row — what stands on the foundation is drawn resting above it). Every node name appears EXACTLY ONCE, in its own tier. Arrows point DOWN, from a dependent to its dependency, using only `│ ▼ ├ └ ─` (no other glyph). One parent fanning out to several children: draw a small tree under the parent, `├──▼──` for every child but the last, `└──▼──` for the last. Several parents converging on the same child (a shared dependency, e.g. the foundation scope): write the child ONCE, with a `▼` under each parent's column pointing at that single line. Example — input `[GRAPH]` (уровень 0: infra-base; уровень 1: api, worker; уровень 2: app; рёбра: app → api, worker · api → infra-base · worker → infra-base) renders as: ``` app ▼ ▼ api worker ▼ ▼ infra-base ``` Approval Check. STOP.

Step.Goal: Materialize the minimal infra-base spec if tooling was declared.
Step.Action:
No tooling declared → skip. Else, per `AX_INFRA_BASE_BOOTSTRAP`, `READ_AND_USE_DIRECTIVE("ai/directives/sdd-v2/formats/infra-base-minimal-spec.xml")`, then scaffold the file via the CLI — infrastructureManifest ToolCall below (it creates directories itself and prints the section manifest; writing the spec from a blank Write instead of the scaffold is the same violation as hand-writing the portal skeleton) — and fill the skeleton to that format (scope-type infrastructure, one-sentence Vision, Tool Stack table, note pointing to `discovery infra-base` for the full Decision Log — the bootstrap only locks the tool choice, the full `infra` flow comes later). Approval Check. STOP.
npx gennady sdd-new infrastructure --scope infra-base Use infrastructureManifest.

When `specs/README.md` does not exist yet, create its skeleton via portalManifest ToolCall below first — it never overwrites and prints the section manifest (which sections are REQUIRED and what to fill); when it already exists, edit it in place, skip `sdd-new`. The portal skeleton is its format: fill the structured Vision block confirmed at STEP_1 (target-state paragraph plus Для кого / Боль / Успех / Принципы), and, per `AX_DECISION_LOG_REQUIRED`, a Decision Log row for every deferred or release-boundary decision routed there in the same step — the section is omitted only when STEP_1 routed no such decision. Scope status (✅ / 🚧) comes from `sdd-state` (presence of `specs//.spec.md`), not a manual stat — rows per `AX_SCOPE_TABLE_FORMAT`. Reconcile any placeholder rows left by the scope flow into full rows — root is the primary owner of `specs/README.md` and the only flow that rewrites it (`AX_PORTAL_PRIMARY_OWNER`). Write the file. Then run integrityCheck ToolCall below to verify portal integrity — graph acyclicity, graph↔table↔spec coherence, no orphan specs or dangling scope references — and resolve any finding before finishing, per `AX_CLOSE_WITH_INTEGRITY_CHECK`.
Gate on NEW content only, never on a recap: the assembled Portal is not new when it only restates what the operator already approved earlier in THIS session — the Vision confirmed at STEP_1, the Scope Graph confirmed at STEP_2, the Tool Stack confirmed at STEP_3. New means anything the operator has not yet approved this session — a Scopes-table description written during assembly, an editorial rewording of an approved sentence, a Decision Log row filed here that STEP_1 did not already surface. When assembly introduced nothing new, show the written result plus the `sdd-check` output and go straight to the continuity menu below — skip the Approval Check; re-confirming a portal built entirely from already-approved pieces asks the operator to re-approve zero new information. When assembly did introduce something new, do not gate on the whole portal either — surface ONLY the delta («при сборке добавил: `` — ок?») and let the operator confirm that delta alone.
The flow never ends on bare text telling the operator to run `/sdd` themselves — close per `NEXT_STEP_MENU_FORMAT`: one ✅ line (portal written, integrity checked), then ONE `AskUserQuestion`. Option 1, recommended while any scope still lacks a spec: «Продолжить спеки: discovery `<следующий скоуп по графу зависимостей>`» — the first UNSPEC'D scope in Scope Graph dependency order (the level-0 / foundation scope, e.g. `infra-base` when present, else the lowest-level scope just added). On this pick, hand control to that scope's branch of the router's own `LOGIC_SWITCH` immediately. The next owner reconstructs context from the portal and specs; no session handoff is required. A scaffold option is offered instead ONLY once every scope in the graph already has a spec — per `NEXT_STEP_MENU_FORMAT` it is never recommended over an outstanding spec (specs need the operator's judgment, scaffold decomposes only approved specs). Selecting it loads scaffold. «Пауза — продолжу позже» stops after printing `/sdd` plus the next scope/step; durable files make that safe. When no work remains, report completion. No terminal state machine or close command exists.
npx gennady sdd-new portal Use portalManifest. npx gennady sdd-check --all . Use integrityCheck.

SddRoot.ChatOutput:
Service line — dim, internal, never narrated (per `AX_NO_PROCESS_NARRATION`): `🗺️ ROOT_R · · · conf=`. Breadcrumb milestones for this flow (per `BREADCRUMB_FORMAT`): Vision · Scope Graph · Infra · Portal.
A step-boundary / decision message (the decision card) is sectioned with markdown headers, in this order. Skip any section empty for this step. During free dialogue inside a step the agent does NOT print this layout — it just talks.
`` — internal anchor + scope + mode + confidence (supplied by the branch)
`` — per `BREADCRUMB_FORMAT`, its OWN paragraph (a blank line above it, not just a `\n`) — markdown collapses a single newline into a space, so without the blank line the breadcrumb visually fuses onto the service line
## `` `` — одной фразой, что делаем
### 🤔 Как я понял задачу — an italic blockquote (`> _…_`), 2–3 sentences max: the task retold in the agent's own words plus the single riskiest assumption, linked by wording to the question that resolves it; never a restate of already-settled content — only what is NEW or could be misread (goes at the TOP) ### 🎯 Главное решение — the crux in plain words; if the decision is a flow (data moving, state transitions, start/stop conditions), add a small ASCII diagram — the one place a fenced block is allowed in this message, at most one per message ### 💡 <О чём решаем> — per `QUESTION_RULE_SLIM` (full format with worked examples lives in `QUESTION_FORMAT`, in the interview / vision directives) ### ↓ Детали — по желанию — reasoning, full comparison, change-list (per `AX_PROGRESSIVE_DISCLOSURE`)
Glyph dictionary — closed inventory, one assigned meaning each, never a free pick. Every glyph here is chosen to read clearly on BOTH a light and a dark terminal/chat theme — half-tone shading characters (`░ ▒ ▓` and similar) are forbidden anywhere in this layout: they render as near-invisible or vanish outright depending on theme.
Section-header glyphs (fixed, one per header, in the order above): - `🤔` — the agent's own understanding check, at the top of a decision card - `🎯` — the crux decision, in plain words - `💡` — a decision the agent is proposing for the operator to confirm or pick between - `↓` — folded detail, expand on demand
Step-TYPE glyphs (fixed, keyed by the step's TYPE, used in the service line / breadcrumb, never a free pick): - `🏗` — creation / scaffold (new spec, new tickets, new files) - `🔍` — audit / review (fresh-eyes read, no write) - `🔧` — fix / reconcile (spec ⟷ code drift repair) - `⚡` — execute (a task ticket's phases running) - `🗺` — routing / overview (intent classification, project-level map)
Breadcrumb-status glyphs (per `BREADCRUMB_FORMAT`): `✅` done · `👷` active · `◻️` not yet.
No other emoji appear in message or section headers — the glyphs enumerated above are the only ones this layout permits.
One line, its own paragraph below the service line — a blank line separates the two (per `MESSAGE_LAYOUT`); a single `\n` with no blank line is a contract defect, markdown renders it fused onto the service line as one run-on. This session's milestones, each rendered ` `, with a status marker chosen for legibility on BOTH light and dark themes — no half-tone shading characters (`░ ▒ ▓`) anywhere, they vanish depending on theme. Status set: `✅` done · `👷` active (the step running now) · `◻️` not yet reached. Delta only; never re-list everything already settled. This is the «where are we», and it replaces a verbose run-on of finished steps.
`Vision ✅ · Scope Graph 👷 · Infra ◻️ · Portal ◻️`
The agent's compressed read of the task — its own confirmation of blind spots so the operator can catch a misread. A `### 🤔 Как я понял задачу` section near the TOP, then an italic blockquote, 2–3 sentences: the essence + the single riskiest assumption, with the assumption linked to the question that resolves it BY WORDING — there are no question numbers or IDs left to point at, so name the question itself. Never a restate of settled content.
### 🤔 Как я понял задачу > квинтэссенция — что считаю главным. > **Где могу ошибаться:** самое хрупкое допущение — это вопрос «<формулировка вопроса>».
When a decision is about a flow — data moving, state transitions, start / stop conditions — draw a tiny ASCII diagram; one glance beats a paragraph. This is the one place a fenced block is allowed inside an operator message (alignment matters). Keep it small.
``` [сеть] [auth] [конфиг] ──всё есть──► ОПРОС идёт ▲ │ └──── снова есть ──── ПАУЗА ◄───────┘ что-то пропало ```
Render after the current artifact is written and verified:
1. One concise line names the produced artifact paths and exact checks that passed. 2. `**Что дальше?**` with 2–4 concrete options derived from current repository artifacts. While a scope in the dependency graph lacks an approved spec, recommend the next spec. Offer scaffold only when all intended specs have approval #1. Scaffold means creation and validation of actual tickets, not implementation. 3. A selected chained option loads its owner directly with exact artifact paths. No hidden session context is transferred; the next owner reconstructs state from specs, tickets, Execution Log, Git, and tool output. 4. «Пауза — продолжу позже» prints one short resume instruction containing the next skill and scope/Task-ID. Pause is always safe because durable artifacts are complete enough to resume. 5. When no chained work remains, report completion. There is no terminal state token and no session close command.
Decision first, reasoning on demand. The must-read top of a message is short: where we are + my read + what to decide. Everything heavy — full option comparison, evidence, the change-list, derivations — goes BELOW a `### ↓ Детали — по желанию` header. Never dump reasoning above the questions. Facts already verified collapse to one line («сверился: …»); uncertainties that need the operator BECOME the questions — never list them twice.

ArtifactOutput.Contract:
One line per entry — no Status/Recorded fields, no multi-line block. The parenthetical carries only what applies; omit a clause entirely rather than writing it empty.
```markdown -DL-N — (почему: ; отвергнуто: ; риск: ) ```
**ID.** `-DL-` — spec acronym first, exactly like a Task-ID and like `-REQ-` (`REQUIREMENT_ENTRY_FORMAT`); `` is sequential within THIS spec only — the acronym gives global uniqueness, not the number. This is the only grammar for NEW entries. Existing append-only file-local `D-N` entries remain immutable and resolvable as legacy references; never create another; conflicts (a duplicate number inside one spec) are caught mechanically, the same way as for `-REQ-`.
Superseding a prior decision appends `; supersedes: -DL-M` to the parenthetical instead of a separate field — the entry stays one line. `` is the recording date (`YYYY-MM-DD`); status (active / superseded / rejected / deferred) is implicit from prose and from whether a later entry supersedes this one — a spec has no dangling "rejected" or "deferred" entries sitting as if active, the prose says so directly (e.g. `отвергнуто в пользу X` folded into the same line that would have recorded it, never a standalone rejected entry with its own `-DL-N`).
